clue.text: Obscure work leads to a doubt, lines being missing

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: RY is the usual abbreviation for railway lines, so those letters drop out of the word for a doubt

parts.note: a query is a doubt or question

explanation.surface: A piece of work is so cryptic it leaves the reader uncertain, with some lines apparently lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines being missing' takes RY (railway) out of QUERY, leaving QUE; 'leads to' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something opaque cannot be seen through or understood, which is what obscure means.

clue.text: Clerk in enclosure with court official keeping quiet

indicators.note: the two pieces hold the letter for quiet between them

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure for animals
an usher keeps order in a law court
p is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A clerk stands in a pen while a court officer keeps silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is a disparaging term for an office clerk doing routine paperwork.

clue.text: Music group rather tame initially, some number being drowned

indicators.note: the number letter is submerged inside the other pieces

parts.note: quite means rather, fairly
n stands for an unspecified number in maths

indicators.note: just the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A band is fairly dull at first, with one of its songs lost in the noise.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes inside QUITE plus T (first of 'tame'), between I and T.
explanation.definitionFit: A quintet is a group of five musicians playing together.

clue.text: Pond creature remained as lake vanished

indicators.note: the lake letter disappears from the word for remained

parts.note: left means remained, as in what was left
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A creature stayed behind when its lake dried up.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, a small amphibian found in ponds.

clue.text: Overpowering academic bully, no leader

parts.note: prof is short for professor, a university academic

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for bully is dropped, as a group without its head

parts.note: to pound is to batter or bully

explanation.surface: A domineering professor who bullies others, with no one in charge to stop it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no leader' removes the P from POUND, leaving OUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A profound feeling is intense and deep, strong enough to overwhelm, so the adjectives are close synonyms.

clue.text: Minister about to be given superior accommodation

indicators.note: in a down answer the lodging word is placed above the word for about

parts.note: a pad is a flat or lodging
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A clergyman is about to be offered better lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A padre is a chaplain, a minister of religion, especially in the armed forces.

clue.text: Old boy on solitary trail is on the way out

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
sole means single or solitary
a scent is a trail followed by hounds

explanation.surface: A former pupil walking a lonely path is dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolescent is becoming outdated and falling out of use.

clue.text: Excess across a period of time

parts.note: over means across, as in over the road
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Too much spread across a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An overage is a surplus, an amount beyond what is needed or expected.

clue.text: Our country, in terrible end, zapped into oblivion?

indicators.note: the country's letters go inside the rearranged word
the word end is mangled into a new order

parts.note: for a British newspaper, our country is the UK

explanation.surface: Fears of a dreadful fate for Britain, wiped out by a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that zapped normally means microwaved; here it is read as wiped out by a nuclear strike, and 'terrible' gives NED from the word end.
explanation.definitionFit: To nuke is to destroy with nuclear weapons, wiping a place out entirely.

clue.text: One's soon brought round yob to be ceremonially blessed

indicators.note: the word for soon is put around the numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is 'is', a link
a Ted (Teddy boy) was a 1950s British youth thought of as a yob

explanation.surface: Someone about to bring a hooligan round so he can be blessed in a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy, or Ted, was a rebellious young British man of the 1950s; 'brought round' puts I inside ANON.
explanation.definitionFit: To anoint is to smear with holy oil in a religious ceremony, a form of consecration or blessing.

clue.text: Ruler making one tremble when speaking

indicators.note: said out loud, the word for making tremble matches the Arab title

parts.note: to shake someone is to make them tremble

explanation.surface: A ruler whose very speech makes subjects quake.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheikh is an Arab chief or ruler of a tribe, family or state.

clue.text: Nothing more than a dandy? That's a relief!

definitions.meaning: a swell is a dandy, so merely one
an exclamation of thankfulness that things turned out for the better

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when an outcome proves fortunate, while respaced it describes someone merely a fashionable dandy.

clue.text: Dusty state capital?

definitions.meaning: Dusty ... was a British pop singer of the 1960s

explanation.definitionFit: The singer Dusty took this surname, and the same name belongs to the capital of Illinois.

clue.text: Carmen? I had to be in that opera

indicators.note: the short form of I had sits inside the motoring club's letters

parts.note: read as car men: the AA (Automobile Association) is Britain's motoring breakdown organisation
I'd is the short form of I had

explanation.surface: A question of whether the singer playing Carmen once performed in a particular opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carmen' looks like Bizet's opera, which tempts as the definition; it splits as car men, the AA, Britain's motoring breakdown service.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdi's Aida is a famous opera, so it names the work referred to here.

clue.text: Go and howl having abandoned university

indicators.note: the yell has lost the letter for university, leaving it behind

parts.note: to shout is to howl or yell

explanation.surface: Someone told to have a try and yell after dropping out of college.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a go and having a shot both mean making an attempt at something.

clue.text: Restaurant's rubbish is leading to endless row

definitions.note: the definition is a restaurant, the 's standing for 'is' linking it to the wordplay

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish

indicators.note: the word for a row loses its final letter

parts.note: a series is a row or sequence

explanation.surface: A diner's food is so bad it causes a never-ending argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel but means a line, SERIES, which 'endless' cuts to SERIE; 'leading to' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a restaurant specialising in meat roasted on a turning spit.

clue.text: Organisation that used to provide flight for couple at Prestwick

definitions.text: Organisation that used to provide flight
definitions.meaning: Trans World Airlines, a defunct US airline
Prestwick is in Scotland, where the Scots word for two is used

explanation.definitionFit: The letters name the former American airline and are also the Scots word meaning two.

clue.text: Those folk excellent in pub generally

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
them refers to those people
A1 means first-rate, written here as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: Those people are generally fine in their local.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, first-class, is written AI, the 1 as I.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on the whole, mostly, as generally does.

clue.text: It's the practice of a robber dressing to conceal equipment

indicators.note: the gear is hidden away inside the wound dressing

parts.note: a bandage is a dressing for a wound
rig is gear or equipment

explanation.surface: A thief wears a disguise to hide their tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigandage is robbery and plunder carried out by bandits, so it is a brigand's way of life.

clue.text: Yellow ducks and drakes perhaps crossing marsh

indicators.note: the game word spans the marsh, lying across it on both sides

parts.note: ducks and drakes, skimming stones on water, is an example of a game
a bog is a marsh

explanation.surface: Yellow-billed ducks and drakes flying over a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks and drakes' suggests waterfowl but is the stone-skimming game.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamboge is a deep yellow pigment made from tree resin.

clue.text: Shelter and bed — first requirement for everybody

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is needed

explanation.surface: Housing and a place to sleep are the basic needs of everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A cote is a small shelter for animals or birds, such as a dovecote.

clue.text: Party that is set up with unruly child kept outside

indicators.note: the scrambled word is held around the outside of the other piece
the letters of child run wild into another order
in a down answer the abbreviation is turned to read upwards

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A party organised with a badly behaved child left outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' signals a reversal in a down answer, and 'unruly' scrambles the child letters into C...LIDH, which wrap around the turned abbreviation; a ceilidh is a Gaelic dance gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish social gathering with folk music and dancing.

clue.text: Totally inadequate, or excellent?

indicators.note: the word falls short of its full length, losing its last letter

parts.note: plumb, as in plumb crazy, means completely or totally

explanation.surface: A question of whether something is hopelessly poor or first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totally inadequate' reads as one phrase meaning dreadful, but 'Totally' is PLUMB and 'inadequate' cuts its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum job or role is a highly desirable, excellent one, so the word is used as an adjective.

clue.text: Large old ship's very slow movement

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A big ancient vessel moving very slowly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Argo carried Jason and the Argonauts.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical direction for a very slow tempo, and a piece played that way.

clue.text: Company falling short — more sedate person needed in emergency

indicators.note: the company word comes up short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a firm is a business company
staider is the comparative of staid, sedate

explanation.surface: A business underperforms, so a calmer person is brought in for the crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-aider is someone trained to give immediate care when an accident or emergency happens.

clue.text: Bird appearing in our avenue

indicators.note: the letters show up within the words our avenue

explanation.surface: A bird has been spotted in the street where we live.
explanation.definitionFit: A raven is a large black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Audibly tolerate Rupert

indicators.note: the word for tolerate is heard rather than seen, giving the poet's surname

parts.note: to brook is to tolerate or put up with

explanation.surface: Something about putting up with a man named Rupert, out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Brooke was an English poet of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert Brooke was the English war poet, so the forename leads to his surname.

clue.text: Unblemished instrument

definitions.meaning: a small keyboard instrument of the harpsichord family, popular in the 16th century

explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means chaste and unspoilt; as a noun it is an early harpsichord-like keyboard.

clue.text: Street violence? Time to leave port

indicators.note: the time letter departs from the word for street violence

parts.note: a riot is violent disorder in the streets

explanation.surface: Trouble on the streets, so it is time to get out of the harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian seaport.

clue.text: Greek god poisoned mysteriously

indicators.note: the letters of the word are rearranged in a puzzling way

explanation.surface: A deity from Greek myth has been mysteriously given poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Greek god of the sea, earthquakes and horses.

clue.text: Wedding ring is normally available for use

definitions.meaning: a wedding ring is usually worn upon a finger of the hand
ready and at the ready, nearby when needed

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means ready nearby when needed, and also literally describes where a ring is worn, upon the hand.
